Fear Index Hits 37. What Happens Next?

2026-11-20

Subscribe for one money story a week

About this video

Wall Street's fear index, the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), closed at 37.37 on Nov 20, 2026, up from 15.01 on Oct 6, the day the S&P 500 set its record. The S&P 500 fell 7 days in a row to 6,910.39, 11.6% below that record. We explain what the VIX measures, how rare readings like this are (30+ on about 8% of days since 1990), and what the S&P 500 did after each of the 22 times since 1990 that the VIX first closed above 30: higher a month later 15 of 22 times, higher a year later 14 of 21 times (median +15%), with 2008 as the big exception. 0:00 Intro: the fear index 0:50 What is the VIX? 1:37 What it means in dollars 2:11 How high is 30? 2:40 Why it just jumped 3:16 A seesaw 3:35 Why investors are nervous 4:04 Every spike above 30 4:36 What stocks did next 5:03 Four fear spikes 5:49 It already happened this year 6:17 Best and worst days 6:40 What to watch next 7:02 What it means for you 7:35 Recap Sources: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the Cboe Volatility Index (^VIX, from 1990), the S&P 500 (^GSPC) and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC), saved Nov 20, 2026 after the close. FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): DGS10 (10-year Treasury yield), CPIAUCSL (CPI). Spike and return statistics are our calculations, prices only (no dividends). When fear moves that fast, it usually means investors are scrambling to protect themselves all at once. Here's the pattern to remember: the VIX and the stock market usually move like a seesaw. When stocks fall, fear goes up. When stocks rise, fear goes down. Since 1990, on 77 percent of the days the S&P 500 fell, the VIX rose. That's why people call it the fear index. Of the 20 best days for the S&P 500 since 1990, 19 came when the VIX was already at 30 or higher. And of the 20 worst days, 17 did too. The biggest days, good and bad, cluster in fearful markets. So if fear makes you sell, you risk being out of the market on exactly the days that tend to matter most. So what should you watch from here? First, the VIX itself. What does this mean for you? A high VIX means bigger swings, and swings cut both ways: some of the biggest up days come during fearful weeks. Your time horizon matters most: money you need soon carries more risk in a market like this. An emergency fund means you never have to sell at a bad time.
